promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Oct 18 2026, 2 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Keep the long short, the quality sharp, and the volume steady for race freshness.

answers.question: The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?
answers.answer: Yes, a 15‑mile long this week and a 20‑mile long next week will give you the mileage you need while keeping your legs fresh for the race. You don’t need to add a 22‑mile now – keep the peak workouts clean and you’ll be ready.

new.analysis: The athlete is two weeks from the race, in the peak phase.  He has only done one 20‑mile long, so we’ll keep volume moderate, still include a quality session, and run a 15‑mile long this week.  The question asks whether there’s time for a 22‑mile long; we’ll reassure him that a 15‑mile long now and a 20‑mile long next week will give enough mileage without over‑exertion.  No medical red flags, so no safety callouts.  The plan will have rest on Mon, easy runs on Tue/Thu, a quality on Wed, easy Saturday, long on Sun.  Flags focus on monitoring long distance, quality effort, recovery, heart‑rate drift, and total volume.
